full_judgment: 13. Mr Amit Das Gupta the learned Advocate for the opposite party Nos. 1-5 submits that the suit is misconceived baseless and are not tenable in law and this opposite parties as the real owner of the suit property is the necessary parties to the suit land. The learned Advocate further submits that the suit property situated within Mohammadpur Housing Estates, Block-C, Plot No. 26/17 comprising an area of 1147.77 Sq, yds belonged to one Abdul Kuddus who owned the said property by the registered deed No. 18221 dated 12-12-1968 and the said Abdul Kuddus died leaving his two wives namely Masuda Begum and Delwara Begum Parul and he had no son or daughter. During his life time he adopted a daughter named Sultana Bilkis Munni who ultimately got no right title and interest in the suit property and after his death according to Islamic Shariah law of inheritance his properties are inherited by his wives Masuda Begum and Delwara Begum Parul, his three Brothers Ali Arshad, Serajul Haque and Suruj Miah and his sister Anwara Begum. Due to a dispute regarding partition of the properties of Abdul Kuddus his second wife Delwara Begum Parul filed Title Suit No. 54 of 2007 before the Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka for partition of the properties of deceased Abdul Kuddus where Masuda Begum and these Opposite Parties are made parties in the category of defendants. Thereafter the suit on transfer is renumbered as Title Suit No. 72 of 2013 and pending before the learned Joint District Judge, Additional Court Dhaka. The learned Advocate lastly submits that Mosaraf Hossain Chowdhury in collusion with Masuda Begum and Sultana Bilkis Munni created a deed of sale being No. 9847 dated 22-10-2006 in favour of him and thereafter he through his attorney namely Md Harun-or-Rashid created another collusive deed of agreement for sale i.e. the sale deed for grabbing the suit property. The said deeds are created inasmuch as the said Masuda Begum had only one anna share over the suit property and on the other hand the said Sultana Bilkis Munni being an adopted daughter of deceased Abdul Kuddus had no right title and interest over the suit property and it is to be mentioned here that the opposite parties have already filed a suit for cancellation of the void deed of sale being No. 9867 dated 22-10-2006 before the learned Joint District Judge, 2nd Court, Dhaka being Title Suit No. 355 of 2012 which is pending for disposal. The learned Advocate in course of his submissions refers the case of Golam Kader being dead his heirs Nurun Nahar Begum vs Abdul Khaleque Choukder reported in 43 DLR (AD) 107 where their Lordships of our Apex Court held that " Addition of party in a suit for Specific Performance of Contract-the appellants averments in the application for addition of party setting up an independent title to the land disentitle them to be included as parties within the framework of the present suit wherein the real question to be determined is whether the contract for sale between the parties therein was genuine and whether on the basis thereof the plaintiffs are entitled to get a decree. The averments for addition of party will convert the present suit into one for determination of title which is not permissible in law". The same principle has also been adopted in the case of Buliara Begum vs Md Abu Taher Mia as decided by a Division Bench of this Hon'ble Division in Civil Revision No. 5899 of 2001. On the contrary the learned Advocate appearing for the opposite parties relied upon his submissions on the basis of the case of Ejahar Miah vs Shahar Banu reported in 49 DLR (AD) 85. The citations as referred by the learned Advocate appearing for the petitioners in support of his contention are fully applicable in the facts and circumstances of the present case on the contrary the citation as referred by the learned Advocate for the opposite parties in support of his contention has no manner of application in the facts and circumstances of the present case.
